tested_on.host: Hermes agent on an openclawlaunch Linux container: 16 vCPU, 62 GiB RAM, 39 GB free disk at slice start (headless-Linux numbers; real-device behavior is NOT_RUN)

A01.notes: Clean checkout build (tsc --noEmit + vite build + verified OCR asset fetch) succeeds; the built dist/ serves and renders the home screen with zero console errors in both engines.

A02.notes: Real in-browser OCR (tesseract.js in its own worker, same-origin assets, verified eng.traineddata.gz) on fixture clean01; review screen shows the extracted text in both engines.

A03.notes: navigator.share spied (OS share sheet not automatable, A27): payload.text equals the review text exactly. Chromium verifies Copy with a real granted clipboard read; Playwright WebKit grants no clipboard permissions and readText is platform-denied, so the clipboard content is verified there with a real paste round-trip (writeText needs no permission; see runner-smoke.md). The native share sheet on a real device remains NOT_RUN (A27).

A20.notes: Clean-set mean CER through the full app pipeline: 1.33% in Chromium and 1.33% in WebKit (bar <= 5%). Per-fixture: clean01=1.15% clean02=0.67% clean03=1.57% clean04=1.32% clean05=1.49% clean06=1.78%, identical across engines. Engine selection by measurement incl. rejected candidates: docs/evidence/S0/ocr_engine_comparison.md (bench CER 2.31% on raw engine output; app-level normalization narrows it to 1.33%).

verify.evidence: run on the final tree; output in the slice PR

limitations: The OS share sheet itself is not automatable; navigator.share is spied and its payload asserted (A27 real-device checks remain NOT_RUN by design).

Playwright's WebKit on Linux cannot grant clipboard permissions; readText is platform-denied there. Copy is verified in WebKit via a real paste round-trip, and by a real granted clipboard read in Chromium.
WebKit-on-Linux is not iOS Safari; no real-device claim is made anywhere.
OCR accuracy is measured on the synthetic fixture set (clean-set CER 1.33%); it does not prove accuracy on arbitrary real screenshots.

The LLM cleanup, storage audits, paste/share-target, installability, and model manager are S1+ slices; the OCR engine assets (worker/core/traineddata) are fetched at build time and served same-origin, while app-shell caching lands with the PWA slice (S2).
